That is, the law of those before him was likewise: prophets used to marry many virgin women and women divorced by others. ﴿And ever is the command of Allah a decree determined⁠ ⁠﴾: that is, everything is by decree and predestination. Qadar means determination, and between "maf'ul" (what is done) and "maqdur" (what is determined) there is a distinction that is commonly stated between qada' (decree) and qadar (predestination). Qada' is what was intended originally, and qadar is what becomes a consequence of it. An example: one who intends a city and alights on the road to that city at a caravanserai or village; it is correct, by custom, that when someone asks, "Why did you come to this village?" he replies, "I did not come to this one; I intended the such-and-such city, and this one fell on my way," even though he has arrived there and entered it. Knowing this, all good is by qada', and whatever harm is in the world is by qadar. Allah, exalted is He, created the responsible person such that he desires and becomes angry, so that his striving to dominate intellect and religion over them is rewarded in the most complete manner. In some cases this led to fornication and killing, yet Allah did not create them in him with killing and fornication as the intended aim, though this occurs by the qadar of Allah.

Knowing this, in His saying, exalted is He, first, ﴿And ever is the command of Allah accomplished⁠ ⁠﴾, and second, ﴿And ever is the command of Allah a decree determined⁠ ⁠﴾, there is a subtle point: when He said, ﴿We married her to you⁠ ⁠﴾, He said ﴿And ever is the command of Allah accomplished⁠ ⁠﴾, meaning our marriage of Zaynab to you was intended, primary, decreed, and observed. And when He said ﴿the practice of Allah with those who passed on⁠ ⁠﴾, as an indication of the story of Dawud, peace be upon him, when he was tempted by the woman of Uriah, He said ﴿And ever is the command of Allah a decree determined⁠ ⁠﴾, meaning that was a subsidiary ruling. If someone said: this is the view of the Mu'tazilah regarding generation (tawlid) and the philosophers regarding the necessity of things occurring in certain ways, like fire burning, since they said Allah, exalted is He, willed to create what ripens things, and it can only be burning by nature, so He created fire for benefit, and then a chance combination of causes occurred that caused the house of Zayd or the house of 'Amr to burn. We say: God forbid that we say Allah is not choosing in His acts, or that something happens not by His choice. Rather, the people of the Sunnah say: Allah established His custom that such-and-such occurs, meaning He is able to create fire such that when meat is needed to be cooked, it cooks, and when the garment of an old woman touches it, it does not burn. Do you not see that it did not burn Ibrahim, peace be upon him, despite its strength and abundance? Rather He created it in a different manner by pure will, or for a hidden wisdom, and He is not questioned about what He does.

We say: whatever is in the course of His custom, exalted is He, in a way that human intellects grasp, we say: by decree. And whatever occurs in a way that a deficient intellect might ask why it was so and why it was not otherwise, we say: by predestination.

Likewise, if she is in the waiting period, he still has a connection with her, since it is possible that the womb is occupied, so he has not yet fulfilled his need from her. But when he divorces and her waiting period ends, he has become independent of her and no connection with her remains, so he has fulfilled his need from her. This accords with what is in the Sharia, because marrying the wife of another, or one who is in his waiting period, is not permissible. Therefore He said, ﴿when [Zayd] had no longer any need⁠ ⁠﴾. Likewise is His saying: ﴿in order that there not be upon the believers any discomfort concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they have no longer any need for them⁠ ⁠﴾,

meaning: when they have divorced them and their waiting periods have ended. Qada' is what was intended originally, and qadar is what becomes a consequence of it. An example: one who intends a city and alights on the road to that city at a caravanserai or village; it is correct, by custom, that when someone asks, "Why did you come to this village?" he replies, "I did not come to this one; I intended the such-and-such city, and this one fell on my way," even though he has arrived there and entered it. Allah, exalted is He, created the responsible person such that he desires and becomes angry, so that his striving to dominate intellect and religion over them is rewarded in the most complete manner. And when He said ﴿the practice of Allah with those who passed on⁠ ⁠﴾, as an indication of the story of Dawud, peace be upon him, when he was tempted by the woman of Uriah, He said ﴿And ever is the command of Allah a decree determined⁠ ⁠﴾, meaning that was a subsidiary ruling. If someone said: this is the view of the Mu'tazilah regarding generation (tawlid) and the philosophers regarding the necessity of things occurring in certain ways, like fire burning, since they said Allah, exalted is He, willed to create what ripens things, and it can only be burning by nature, so He created fire for benefit, and then a chance combination of causes occurred that caused the house of Zayd or the house of 'Amr to burn. Rather, the people of the Sunnah say: Allah established His custom that such-and-such occurs, meaning He is able to create fire such that when meat is needed to be cooked, it cooks, and when the garment of an old woman touches it, it does not burn. Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Muhammad is not the father of any one of your men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the seal of the prophets. And Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.﴾

When Allah explained the benefits in the Prophet's (ﷺ) marriage to Zaynab, He clarified that it was free of the aspects of corruption. That is because the corruption that might be imagined was confined to marrying the wife of a son, which is not permissible. So Allah, exalted is He, said: Indeed, Zayd was not a son of his. Rather, none of the men was a son of Muhammad. If someone says: the Prophet was the father of one of the men, because "rajul" (man) is the term for a male among the offspring of Adam, and Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if they are siblings, men and women﴾ [an-Nisa: 176], and a boy is included in that. The first: in usage, "rajul" (man) includes in its meaning maturity and adulthood, and the Prophet (ﷺ) had no grown son who would be called a man.

Then, when Allah, exalted is He, negated his being a father, He followed it with what indicates the establishment of something that has the ruling of fatherhood in some respects, saying: ﴿but he is the Messenger of Allah﴾. For the Prophet is closer to the believers than their own selves, and a father is not like that. Then he clarified what adds to the increase of compassion on his part and reverence on their part, by saying: ﴿and the seal of the prophets﴾. That is because a prophet after whom there is another prophet, if he leaves out something of the advice and clarification, the one who comes after him makes it up. But one after whom there is no prophet is more compassionate to his nation, more guiding to them, and more beneficial, as he is like a parent to his child who has no one else at all.

That is because the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) conveys legislation, but if he himself refrains from it, a aversion remains in some souls. Do you not see that by his saying he indicated the permissibility of eating the lizard (ḍabb), and then, when he did not eat it, something remained in people's souls? And when he ate the flesh of the camel, its eating became good, although in some faiths it is not eaten. Likewise the hare.

That is because the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) conveys legislation, but if he himself refrains from it, a aversion remains in some souls. Do you not see that by his saying he indicated the permissibility of eating the lizard (ḍabb), and then, when he did not eat it, something remained in people's souls? * * *
Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance﴾.

The connection of this verse with what precedes it is that the surah's foundation and structure rest upon the discipline of the Prophet (ﷺ). We have mentioned that Allah, exalted is He, began by mentioning what the Prophet (ﷺ) should be with Allah, which is taqwa (God-consciousness), and mentioned what the Prophet (ﷺ) should be with his family and relatives by saying: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives﴾ [al-Ahzab: 28]. Allah, exalted is He, commands His believing servants with what He commands His prophets and messengers, so He guided His servants just as He disciplined His Prophet, and began with what relates to His side, which is reverence, saying: ﴿O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance﴾, just as He said to His Prophet: ﴿O Prophet, fear Allah﴾.

Here there is also a subtle point: the believer may forget the remembrance of Allah, so he was commanded to remain constant in remembrance. As for the Prophet, being among those brought near, he does not forget; but one brought near to the King may become complacent in his nearness to him, so his fear diminishes. Therefore He said: ﴿fear Allah﴾, for the sincere person is in great danger, and the good deeds of the saints are the sins of the prophets. And His saying: ﴿with much remembrance﴾ — we have mentioned that in many places, when Allah mentions remembrance He describes it as abundant, since there is no obstacle to remembrance, as we have explained.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 33, verse 46:**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And glorify Him morning and evening﴾. That is, when you remember Him, your remembrance of Him should be in a manner that exalts Him and declares Him free of every imperfection. This is what is meant by *tasbih* (glorification). It has been said that what is meant by it is prayer (*salah*). It has also been said that His glorifying (in the verse) at morning and evening refers to prayer, as an indication of constancy. This is because one who intends generality may mention the two extremes and understand the middle from them, as in the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him): "If your first and your last..." He did not mention your middle, and from this exaggeration in generality is understood.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels, that He may bring you out from darkness into light. And He is ever merciful to the believers﴾. He means: He sends blessings upon you and shows mercy to you, while you do not remember Him. So He mentioned His blessing as an incitement for the believers to remember and glorify Him. ﴿That He may bring you out from darkness into light﴾: that is, that He may guide you by His mercy. The blessing from Allah is mercy, and the blessing from the angels is seeking forgiveness. It has been said that a *mushtarak* (homonymous) word may be used in both of its meanings together, and likewise combining the literal and the figurative sense in one word is permissible. This view is attributed to al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, and it is not far-fetched. If one wishes to bring it closer so that it becomes very near, we say: mercy and seeking forgiveness both share concern for the state of the one who is shown mercy and the one for whom forgiveness is sought, and the intended meaning is that common element. Thus the indication is by implication (*tadammun*), since concern is a part of both. ﴿And He is ever merciful to the believers﴾: this is good news for all the believers, and an indication that His saying ﴿He sends blessings upon you﴾ is not restricted to those who were present at the time of revelation.

﴿Their greeting on the day they meet Him will be, "Peace." And He has prepared for them a noble reward﴾

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Their greeting on the day they meet Him will be "Peace"﴾. When Allah had explained His concern (for them) in the first (life), He explained His concern in the Hereafter. He mentioned greeting with peace because it is the indicator of good things. Whoever meets another and greets him with peace indicates friendship between them, and if he does not greet him, that indicates hostility. His saying ﴿on the day they meet Him﴾ means the Day of Resurrection. This is because a person in his worldly life is not fully turned towards Allah. How could he be, when in his sleep he is heedless of Him, and for most of his time he is busy seeking his provision? In the Hereafter, however, no one has any preoccupation that diverts him from the remembrance of Allah. So that is the true meeting.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And He has prepared for them a noble reward﴾. If someone says: "Preparation is only done by one who is unable, when in need of a thing, to obtain it. But Allah, exalted is He, has no need and no incapacity. So when He meets them, He gives them what pleases them and more. What then is the meaning of preparation beforehand?" We answer: preparation is for honouring, not for need. This is like a king who, when told that a certain man is coming, prepares for him a house and various kinds of honour, and does not say, "When he arrives we will open the treasury and give him what pleases him." Likewise, Allah, for the perfection of honouring, has prepared for the one who remembers Him a noble reward. The meaning of "noble" we have already mentioned regarding provision: that is, He has prepared for him a reward that comes to him without his seeking it, unlike the world, where a person seeks provision a thousand times and does not obtain it except by measure.

His saying ﴿Their greeting on the day they meet Him will be "Peace"﴾ is appropriate to their condition, because when they remembered Allah in their worldly life, knowledge of Him came to them, and when they glorified Him, that knowledge was confirmed, since they knew Him as He should be known, with the attributes of majesty and the qualities of perfection. Allah knew their state in the world, so He treated them kindly with mercy, as He said: ﴿It is He who sends blessings upon you﴾, and He said: ﴿And He is ever merciful to the believers﴾. When two acquainted people meet, and one of them is compassionate toward the other while the other holds him in the highest regard, nothing between them is realized except peace and all kinds of honour.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness, a bringer of good news, and a warner﴾ ﴿and as one who invites to Allah by His permission, and as a illuminating lamp﴾. We have mentioned that the surah contains instruction for the Prophet (peace be upon him) from his Lord. So His saying at its beginning: ﴿O Prophet, fear Allah﴾ is an indication of what he should be with his Lord. His saying: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives﴾ is an indication of what he should be with his family. His saying: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have sent you﴾ is an indication of what he should be with all of creation. His exalted saying ﴿as a witness﴾ admits several meanings:

First: he is a witness over creation on the Day of Resurrection, as He said: ﴿And the Messenger will be a witness over you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143]. According to this, the Prophet was sent as a witness, meaning one who bears testimony, and in the Hereafter he will be a witness, meaning one who delivers what he bore.

Second: he is a witness that there is no god but Allah. According to this there is a subtle point: Allah made the Prophet a witness to the Oneness (of God), and a witness is not a claimant. Allah did not make the Prophet a claimant regarding the matter of Oneness, because a claimant is one who says something contrary to the apparent, whereas the Oneness of God is more evident than the sun. The Prophet (peace be upon him) had claimed prophethood, so Allah made Himself a witness for him in return for his being a witness for Allah. So He said: ﴿And Allah knows that you are indeed His Messenger﴾.

Third: he is a witness in this world concerning the states of the Hereafter, such as Paradise, Hell, the Balance and the Bridge, and he is a witness in the Hereafter concerning the states of this world, regarding obedience and disobedience, righteousness and corruption.

His saying ﴿a bringer of good news and a warner﴾, and ﴿and one who invites﴾, contains a fine order. This is because the Prophet (peace be upon him) was sent as a witness by his saying: there is no god but Allah, and he encourages this through good news. If that does not suffice, he warns with threat. Then he does not settle for their saying "there is no god but Allah," but calls them to the path of Allah, as He said: ﴿Invite to the way of your Lord﴾ [al-Nahl: 125]. His saying ﴿and as an illuminating lamp﴾ means: one who proves what he says, manifesting it with the clearest proofs. This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿with wisdom and good instruction﴾ [al-Nahl: 125].

In this there are subtle points.

The first: His saying ﴿and as one who invites to Allah by His permission﴾, where He did not say "and as a witness by His permission and a bringer of good news," but for inviting He said "by His permission." This is because one who says of a king that he is king of the world, and no other, does not need permission from him for that, since he has described him with what is in him. Likewise, when one says that whoever obeys him will be happy and whoever disobeys him will be wretched, he is a bringer of good news and a warner and does not need permission from the king for that. But when one says: "Come to his table and attend his feast," he needs permission from him. So He said: ﴿and as one who invites to Allah by His permission﴾.

Another aspect: the Prophet says, "I call to Allah," and the saint (*wali*) also calls to Allah. The first needs no permission from anyone, while the second is authorized by the Prophet (peace be upon him), as He said: ﴿Say: This is my way; I invite to Allah with insight, I and whoever follows me﴾ [Yusuf: 108]. The Prophet (peace be upon him) also said: "May Allah have mercy on a servant who hears my saying and conveys it as he heard it." The Prophet (peace be upon him) is the one authorized by Allah to call to Him without intermediary.

The second subtle point: He said regarding the Prophet (peace be upon him) ﴿and as a lamp﴾, and did not say he is a sun, although the sun is more luminous than a lamp. This is for several benefits. Among them: the light of the sun is not taken from it, whereas from a lamp many lights can be taken. If the first one goes out, the one taken from it remains. Likewise, if the Prophet (peace be upon him) were absent, his light would remain, since every Companion took from him the light of guidance, as the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "My Companions are like the stars: whichever of them you follow, you will be guided." There is also a subtle point in this report, though it is not part of the *tafsir* (exegesis), but speech draws speech: the Prophet (peace be upon him) did not make his Companions like lamps but made them like stars, because a star does not have light taken from it; rather, it has light in itself, and when it sets, no light derived from it remains. Likewise, when a Companion dies, the Successor (*tabi'i*) is illuminated by the light of the Prophet (peace be upon him) and nothing is taken from him except the saying and action of the Prophet (peace be upon him). So the lights of all the mujtahids (independent jurists) come from the Prophet (peace be upon him). Had he made them like lamps while the Prophet (peace be upon him) was also a lamp, it would have been permissible for the mujtahid to be illuminated by whichever of them he wished and to take light from whomever he chose. But that is not the case, for in the presence of a clear text of the Prophet (peace be upon him), one does not act on the saying of a Companion. Light is taken from the Prophet, and it is not taken from a Companion. Thus he did not make them lamps. This points to weakness in the report "the lamp of the Ummah," which the scholars of hadith have mentioned. There is another interpretation of "lamp": that what is meant is the Qur'an, and the sense is: "Indeed We have sent you," and ﴿and a illuminating lamp﴾ is coordinated with the position of the kaf (of "We have sent you" ), meaning: "and We have sent an illuminating lamp." According to our view that it is coordinated with "bringer of good news and warner," its meaning would be: "and [one] of a lamp," because a *hal* (circumstantial qualifier) can only be a description of the doer or the object, and "lamp" is not a description, since the Prophet (peace be upon him) was not literally a lamp. Or it may be like the saying of one who says: "I saw him a lion," meaning "a brave man." So His saying ﴿and as a lamp﴾ means: a guide who clarifies, like a lamp that shows the path and makes the matter clear.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 33, verses 47–49:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And give good tidings to the believers that they will have from Allah a great bounty﴾ is a conjunction with an implied clause, its estimate being: "Indeed We have sent you as a witness and a bearer of good tidings, so bear witness and give good tidings." He did not mention "so bear witness" because it is dispensed with. As for the good tidings, they were mentioned to show nobility, and because they are not obligatory were it not for the command. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿that they will have from Allah a great bounty﴾ is like His saying: "and He has prepared for them a mighty reward." So "mighty" (ʿaẓīm) and "great" (kabīr) are close in meaning. That it is from Allah is great, so how much more so when there is with it another greatness.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and leave off their harm, and rely upon Allah; and sufficient is Allah as a Trustee (wakīl)﴾

This is an indication of warning, meaning: oppose them and refute them. On this basis, His saying: ﴿and leave off their harm﴾ means: leave the matter to Allah, for He will punish them by your hands and by the Fire. What clarifies this is His saying: ﴿and rely upon Allah; and sufficient is Allah as a Trustee﴾, i.e., Allah is sufficient for His servant. Some of the Muʿtazilah said: it is not permissible to name Allah "al-Wakīl" (the Trustee), because the wakīl is lower in rank than the muwakkil (the one who appoints). His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and sufficient is Allah as a Trustee﴾ is a proof against him, and his objection is feeble, in that a trustee may be appointed for exaltation and may be appointed for incapacity, and Allah is the Trustee of His servants because of their incapacity to dispose of affairs. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and sufficient is Allah as a Trustee﴾ becomes clear if you consider the matters for which a single trustee does not suffice: that he is not strong and capable of acting, like a king with many occupations who needs agents because one person cannot take charge of all his affairs; and that he is not knowing of what the appointment concerns; and that he is not rich. Allah, the Exalted, is knowing, capable, and not in need, so He suffices as a Trustee.

* * *

Then the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then there is for you no waiting period (ʿidda) that you should count against them. So provide for them and release them with a fair release.﴾

The connection of this verse with what precedes is that Allah, the Exalted, in this surah mentioned noble morals and disciplined His Prophet according to what we have mentioned. However, Allah, the Exalted, commanded His believing servants with what He commanded His sent Prophet. Thus, whenever He mentioned to the Prophet an act of nobility and taught him a manner, He mentioned to the believers what suits it. Just as Allah began in disciplining the Prophet, peace be upon him, with mention of what relates to the side of Allah, in His saying: ﴿O Prophet, fear Allah﴾, and followed it with what relates to the side of those under his authority, his wives, in His saying after this: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives﴾, and then a third time with what relates to the side of the common people, in His saying: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness﴾, likewise He began in guiding the believers with what relates to the side of Allah, saying: ﴿O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance﴾ [al-Ahzab: 41], then followed it with what relates to the side of those under their authority, in His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women﴾, and then, just as He made a threefold arrangement in disciplining the Prophet regarding the side of the Ummah, He made a threefold arrangement regarding the rights of the believers concerning what relates to the side of their Prophet, saying after this: ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet﴾ [al-Ahzab: 53], and in His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, send blessings upon him﴾ [al-Ahzab: 56]. In the verse there are issues:

The first issue: If the matter is as you have said, that this is guidance regarding what relates to the side of one who is among a person's intimates, why did He single out the divorced women who were divorced before touching (masīs) for mention? We say: This is guidance to the highest degrees of nobility, so that from it what is below it may be known. Its explanation is that when a woman is divorced before touching, no firm covenant has come about between them; for this reason Allah, the Exalted, said regarding the one who has been touched: ﴿And how could you take it back when you have gone in unto one another and they have taken from you a solemn covenant?﴾ [al-Nisa: 21]. If Allah commands enjoyment and kindness with one with whom there is no affection between him and her, then what do you think of one with whom affection has come about through consummation, or whose firmness has been established by the birth of a child between them? The Qur'an is small in size, but if its meanings were derived, pens would not suffice for them and papers would not contain them. This is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So do not say to them, "Uff"﴾ [al-Isra: 23]. Had He said "do not strike them" or "do not revile them," one would suppose it forbidden only for a meaning specific to striking or reviling; but when He said "do not say to them, 'Uff,'" many meanings are known from it. Likewise here: since He commanded kindness with one with whom there is no affection, there is known from it kindness toward the one touched, toward one not yet divorced, and toward one who has borne a child to him.

As for His saying: ﴿when you marry believing women﴾, the specification by mention is guidance that the believer should marry a believing woman, for she is more protective of his religion. As for His saying: ﴿then you divorce them﴾, it is possible to hold by it that making divorce conditional upon marriage is not valid, since divorce in that case could only occur after marriage; and Allah mentioned it with the particle "then" (thumma), which denotes sequence. As for His saying: ﴿then there is for you no waiting period against them﴾, it shows that the waiting period is predominantly the husband's right, though it does not drop by his dropping it, because of what it contains of the right of Allah, the Exalted. As for His saying: ﴿that you count﴾, i.e., that you yourselves complete its number. ﴿So provide for them﴾: it has been said that this is specific to the delegated woman (mufawwada) for whom no dower was fixed, who, if divorced before touching, becomes entitled to a provision (mut'a). It has also been said that it is general, and on this basis it is a command of obligation or a command of recommendation, on which the scholars differed. Among them are those who said it is for obligation, so the provision is obligatory together with half the dower. Among them are those who said it is for recommendation, so it is recommended that he provide her with something alongside the dowry. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and release them with a fair release﴾, the beauty in release is that he does not demand from her what he has given her.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, then there is for you no waiting period (ʿidda) that you should count against them. So provide for them and release them with a fair release.﴾

The connection of this verse with what precedes is that Allah, the Exalted, in this surah mentioned noble morals and disciplined His Prophet according to what we have mentioned. However, Allah, the Exalted, commanded His believing servants with what He commanded His sent Prophet. Thus, whenever He mentioned to the Prophet an act of nobility and taught him a manner, He mentioned to the believers what suits it. Just as Allah began in disciplining the Prophet, peace be upon him, with mention of what relates to the side of Allah, in His saying: ﴿O Prophet, fear Allah﴾, and followed it with what relates to the side of those under his authority, his wives, in His saying after this: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives﴾, and then a third time with what relates to the side of the common people, in His saying: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness﴾, likewise He began in guiding the believers with what relates to the side of Allah, saying: ﴿O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance﴾ [al-Ahzab: 41], then followed it with what relates to the side of those under their authority, in His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, when you marry believing women﴾, and then, just as He made a threefold arrangement in disciplining the Prophet regarding the side of the Ummah, He made a threefold arrangement regarding the rights of the believers concerning what relates to the side of their Prophet, saying after this: ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet﴾ [al-Ahzab: 53], and in His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, send blessings upon him﴾ [al-Ahzab: 56]. In the verse there are issues:

The first issue: If the matter is as you have said, that this is guidance regarding what relates to the side of one who is among a person's intimates, why did He single out the divorced women who were divorced before touching (masīs) for mention? We say: This is guidance to the highest degrees of nobility, so that from it what is below it may be known. Its explanation is that when a woman is divorced before touching, no firm covenant has come about between them; for this reason Allah, the Exalted, said regarding the one who has been touched: ﴿And how could you take it back when you have gone in unto one another and they have taken from you a solemn covenant?﴾ [al-Nisa: 21]. If Allah commands enjoyment and kindness with one with whom there is no affection between him and her, then what do you think of one with whom affection has come about through consummation, or whose firmness has been established by the birth of a child between them? The Qur'an is small in size, but if its meanings were derived, pens would not suffice for them and papers would not contain them. This is like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So do not say to them, "Uff"﴾ [al-Isra: 23]. Had He said "do not strike them" or "do not revile them," one would suppose it forbidden only for a meaning specific to striking or reviling; but when He said "do not say to them, 'Uff,'" many meanings are known from it. Likewise here: since He commanded kindness with one with whom there is no affection, there is known from it kindness toward the one touched, toward one not yet divorced, and toward one who has borne a child to him.

As for His saying: ﴿when you marry believing women﴾, the specification by mention is guidance that the believer should marry a believing woman, for she is more protective of his religion. As for His saying: ﴿then you divorce them﴾, it is possible to hold by it that making divorce conditional upon marriage is not valid, since divorce in that case could only occur after marriage; and Allah mentioned it with the particle "then" (thumma), which denotes sequence. As for His saying: ﴿then there is for you no waiting period against them﴾, it shows that the waiting period is predominantly the husband's right, though it does not drop by his dropping it, because of what it contains of the right of Allah, the Exalted. As for His saying: ﴿that you count﴾, i.e., that you yourselves complete its number. ﴿So provide for them﴾: it has been said that this is specific to the delegated woman (mufawwada) for whom no dower was fixed, who, if divorced before touching, becomes entitled to a provision (mut'a). It has also been said that it is general, and on this basis it is a command of obligation or a command of recommendation, on which the scholars differed. Among them are those who said it is for obligation, so the provision is obligatory together with half the dower. Among them are those who said it is for recommendation, so it is recommended that he provide her with something alongside the dowry. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and release them with a fair release﴾, the beauty in release is that he does not demand from her what he has given her.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives whose bridal payments (ujur) you have given, and those whom your right hand possesses from what Allah has granted you as spoils, and the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts, and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you, and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet and the Prophet wishes to marry her — a privilege for you alone, apart from the believers. He (exalted is He) mentioned to the Prophet, peace be upon him, what is preferable. For a wife who has been given her dower (mahr) is more content of heart than one who has not been given it. A slave woman whom a man has taken captive with his own hand is purer than one whom a man has bought, because her condition is not known. And those relatives of the Prophet, peace be upon him, who emigrated with him are more noble than those who did not emigrate. Among the people there is one who said that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was obliged to give the dower first, because the woman has the right to refuse until she receives her dower, and the Prophet, peace be upon him, would not exact what was not due to him; and intercourse before giving the bridal gift (sadaq) is not lawful, even though it was lawful for us. And how [could it be otherwise], since when the Prophet, peace be upon him, requested something, it was unlawful to refuse what was requested? The apparent point is that the one who initiates the first time is the man, out of the woman's modesty. So if the Prophet, peace be upon him, had requested from the woman submission before the dower, it would follow that it is obligatory and not obligatory, and this is impossible. It is not so for any one of us.

And he said: What confirms this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and a believing woman if she gives herself to the Prophet﴾, meaning that then no dower remains for her, so she becomes like one who has already received her dower. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿if the Prophet wishes to marry her﴾ is an indication that her giving herself requires acceptance along with it. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿a privilege for you alone, apart from the believers﴾. Al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, said: its meaning is the permissibility of intercourse through the gift, and the occurrence of marriage by her utterance, being among your special privileges. Abu Hanifa said: that woman has become exclusively yours as a wife, and one of the Mothers of the Believers, who is not lawful for anyone else ever. The preference may be stated thus: according to this view, specifying the woman who gives herself would serve no purpose, for all his wives are exclusively his; but according to what we have mentioned, the specification becomes meaningful.

His saying: ﴿We know well what We have ordained for them concerning their wives and those whom their right hands possess﴾ means: what We have mentioned is your obligation and ruling with your wives; as for the ruling for your community, its knowledge is with Us, and We will explain it to them. He mentioned this only so that none of the believers would burden himself with what was permitted to the Prophet, peace be upon him, for he had special privileges in marriage not granted to others, and likewise concerning concubines.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿so that there will be no difficulty for you﴾ means: you would be at ease regarding the matter, so no preoccupation of heart remains for you, and the Faithful Spirit descends with the verses upon your free heart, and you convey the messages of your Lord with your earnestness and striving. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ means: He forgives all sins and shows mercy to His servants.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 33, verse 51:

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿You may postpone whom you will of them, and take to yourself whom you will, and whomever you desire of those you have set aside, there is no blame upon you.﴾

When He had explained that what We have mentioned of wives was made lawful for him, He explained that the various forms of association with them were made lawful for him, so that he may be with them as he wishes, and it is not obligatory upon him to divide his time equally (al-qasm). This is because the Prophet, peace be upon him, in relation to his community, stands in the relation of an obeyed master (al-sayyid al-muta'), and a man, even if he is not a prophet, has his wife in the possession of his marriage, and marriage over her is a form of bondage (riqq). So how much more so are the wives of the Prophet, peace be upon him, in relation to him. Therefore they are like those owned (al-mamlukat) by him, and equal division is not obligatory among those owned.

Al-irja' (postponing) is delay (al-ta'khir), and al-iwa' (taking to oneself) is joining (al-damm).

﴿And whomever you desire of those you have set aside﴾ means: if you seek one whom you had left, then there is no blame upon you in anything of that.

As for the one who said that equal division was obligatory, though his view is weak in relation to what is understood from the verse, he said the meaning is: ﴿You may postpone whom you will﴾, that is, you may delay them when you wish, since equal division is not obligatory in the first case, and the husband may choose not to sleep with any one of them; and ﴿whomever you desire of those you have set aside, there is no blame upon you﴾, so begin with whom you wish and complete the rotation. But the first view is stronger.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿That is nearer to their eyes being comforted, and that they will not grieve, and that they will all be pleased with what you give them.﴾

That is: since equal division is not obligatory upon you, and you do not abandon division, ﴿their eyes will be comforted﴾ by your equalizing among them, and they will not grieve, unlike the case if that were obligatory upon you. So on the night you are with one of them, she says: "He came to me not out of desire of his heart, but only out of God's command and His obligation upon him." ﴿And they will be pleased with what you give them﴾ of postponing and taking to yourself, since they have no claim against you, so that they would not be pleased.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And God knows what is in your hearts, and God is ever Knowing, Forbearing.﴾

That is: if they conceal the opposite of what they show, then God knows the inner thoughts of the hearts, for He is All-Knowing. If He does not reprimand them at the moment, let them not be deceived, for He is Forbearing and does not hasten.

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after [this], nor to exchange them for other wives, even if their beauty pleases you, except those whom your right hand possesses. And Allah is ever, over all things, Watchful.﴾

When Allah did not obligate His Prophet to observe equal turns (al-qasm) and commanded him to give his wives the choice, and they chose Allah and His Messenger, He mentioned what He rewarded them with: the prohibition on taking other women in marriage in place of them for the Prophet, peace be upon him, and the prohibition on divorcing them, by His saying: ﴿nor to exchange them for other wives﴾. And in this are several issues:

The first issue: His saying: ﴿It is not lawful for you [to take] women after [this]﴾. The exegetes said: "After them," but the better view is that it means: It is not lawful for you to take women after their choosing Allah and His Messenger, and their being content with what he gives them of union (al-wasl) and abandonment (al-hijran), of deprivation and of being denied.

The second issue: His saying: ﴿nor to exchange them for other wives﴾ indicates the prohibition of divorcing them. For if it were permissible, he could divorce all of them, and after them he would either marry others or not marry. If he did not marry, he would be among the celibates (al-'uzzab), and marriage is a virtue that the Prophet would not abandon; how could he, when he says: "Marriage is my sunnah" (al-nikah sunnati). And if he married others after them, he would have exchanged them for others, and he is prohibited from exchanging.

صفحة ١٩٢
The third issue: Among the exegetes is one who said that the verse contains neither the prohibition of taking other women nor the prohibition of divorcing them. Rather, the meaning is: it is not lawful for you to take women other than those we have mentioned to you from the believing emigrant women, the daughters of your paternal uncles, the daughters of your paternal aunts, the daughters of your maternal uncles, and the daughters of your maternal aunts. As for others from among the People of the Book, it is not lawful for you to marry them. And His saying: ﴿nor to exchange them for other wives﴾ is a prohibition on the practice of the Jahiliyyah, for they used to exchange wife for wife: one of them would give up his wife and take his friend's wife, and give him his own wife in return. On both interpretations, there is disagreement over two issues: first, the prohibition of divorcing his wives; second, the prohibition of marrying People of the Book women. Whoever interprets according to the first holds that divorce is prohibited, and whoever interprets according to the second holds that marrying People of the Book women is prohibited.

The fourth issue: His saying: ﴿even if their beauty pleases you﴾, that is, the beauty of the women. Al-Zamakhshari said: "His saying: ﴿even if [it] pleases you﴾ is in the sense of a circumstantial clause (hal). The subject of the circumstance cannot be His saying: ﴿other wives﴾, due to the extreme indefiniteness in it, and because the subject of a circumstance should not be indefinite. Therefore it is the Prophet, peace be upon him; meaning: it is not lawful for you to take women, nor to exchange them for other wives, while you are pleased with their beauty."

The fifth issue: The apparent meaning of this is that it abrogates what had been established for him, peace be upon him, that whenever he saw a woman and she made an impression on his heart, she would become forbidden to her husband and he would be obligated to divorce her. This ruling is a legal matter: at the beginning of prophethood, the Prophet, peace be upon him, and all the prophets, feel the intense burden (bura'a') of revelation, then they become accustomed to it, and it descends upon them while they converse with their companions, with nothing preventing them from that. So at the beginning Allah permitted [the taking of] whoever made an impression on his heart, to empty his heart and expand his chest, lest his heart be occupied with other than Allah. Then, when he became accustomed to revelation and to the one through whose tongue the revelation came, this was abrogated, either because of his peace be upon him strength to combine the two matters, or because, through the continuity of descent, no familiar worldly matter remained for him, so no attention to other than Allah remained, and thus he had no need for permission to marry whomever his gaze fell upon.

The sixth issue: The scholars differed over whether the prohibition on women for him was abrogated or not. Al-Shafi'i said: it was abrogated, and 'Aisha said: "The Prophet did not die until women had been made lawful for him." On this view, the abrogating text is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and the daughters of your paternal uncles...﴾ and His saying: ﴿and a believing woman...﴾ according to the view of those who say that the Book cannot be abrogated by a solitary report (khabar al-wahid), since the abrogating text is not mutawatir if it is a report.

* * *
Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿except those whom your right hand possesses.﴾ He did not prohibit female slaves for him, because harm does not arise from a female slave; for this reason it is not permitted for a man to combine two co-wives in one house, because equality between them is achieved and quarrelling is possible; but it is permitted to combine a wife with a group of slave women, because there is no equality among them; for this reason they have no right to equal turns with anyone.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And Allah is ever, over all things, Watchful.﴾ That is, Guardian, knowing everything, capable of everything, because guarding is not achieved except by these two.

[Page 193]

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given you for a meal, without waiting for its preparation.﴾

When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned in the third address, ﴿O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness﴾ [al-Ahzab: 45], explaining his condition with his general community, He said to the believers in this address, "do not enter," as guidance for them and an explanation of their attitude toward the Prophet, peace be upon him, in terms of reverence. The condition of the community with the Prophet is of two kinds:

The first: in private, where the obligation is not to disturb him. He explained this by His saying: ﴿do not enter the houses of the Prophet﴾.

The second: in public, where the obligation is to show honor, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace﴾ [al-Ahzab: 56]. His saying ﴿for a meal, without waiting for its preparation﴾ means: do not enter the houses of the Prophet for a meal unless permission is given you.

* * *

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿But when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse and do not linger for conversation. Indeed, that would cause offense to the Prophet, and he is shy of you, but Allah is not shy of the truth. And when you ask his wives for something, ask them from behind a screen. That is purer for your hearts and their hearts. And it is not for you to offend the Messenger of Allah or to marry his wives after him, ever. Indeed, that would be an enormity in the sight of Allah.﴾

When He had explained the Prophet's condition, that he is a caller to Allah, by His saying ﴿and as a caller to Allah﴾ [al-Ahzab: 46], He said here: do not enter unless you are invited, meaning: just as you did not enter the religion except by his call, so likewise do not enter upon him except after his call. His saying ﴿without waiting for its preparation﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl). Its governing word, according to what al-Zamakhshari said, is "do not enter." He said: its implied meaning is "and do not enter the houses of the Prophet except as those given permission, without waiting for [the meal]." There are several issues in this verse:

The first issue: His saying ﴿unless permission is given you for a meal﴾ may either contain an inversion, its meaning being "do not enter for a meal unless permission is given you," so that it is not a prohibition on entering at other than mealtime without permission; or it may contain no inversion, so its meaning is "do not enter unless permission is given you for a meal," and the permission is then conditioned upon being for a meal. If permission is not given you for a meal, entry is not permitted. Thus, if someone is permitted to enter to listen to speech but not to eat, that is not permitted. We say: the intended meaning is the second, so that the prohibition on entering is general. As for the claim that entry is not permitted except by permission for a meal, we say: al-Zamakhshari said the address is to a people who used to come at mealtime and enter without permission, so they were forbidden to enter at that time without permission. But it is better to say the intended meaning is the second, because inversion is contrary to the original form. His saying ﴿for a meal﴾ is a mention of a particular case, so it does not indicate the negation of anything else, especially when it is known that the other cases are similar. For whoever is permitted to enter his house with his permission for a meal is also permitted to enter for other than a meal with his permission, since it is possible for other than a meal to occur together with a meal. For it is permissible to speak with him at the time he invites you to a meal, to ask him to attend to your needs, and to learn from what he has of knowledge along with the provision of food. When he is content with all of this, his contentment with part of it is closer to action. This becomes of the type of ﴿so do not say to them, "Uff"﴾ [al-Isra: 23]. His saying ﴿without waiting for its preparation﴾ means: you should not wait for the time of the meal, for it may not be ready.

[Page 194]

The second issue: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿But when you are invited, then enter﴾ contains a subtle point, namely that customarily, when someone who is accustomed to entering a house without permission is told, "do not enter it unless you have permission," he is offended and withdraws so that he never enters it at all, neither by invitation nor otherwise. So He said: do not do what the arrogant do; rather, be obedient and attentive: when you are told, "do not enter," do not enter; and when you are told, "enter," then enter. As for ﴿inā(hu)﴾, it is said to mean its time, and it is said to mean its readiness. His saying ﴿unless permission is given﴾ indicates permissibility, and His saying ﴿But when you are invited, then enter﴾ indicates obligation. Thus His saying ﴿But when you are invited﴾ is not an emphasis; rather, it conveys a new benefit.

The third issue: Permission does not require explicit verbal statement. Rather, when knowledge of consent is obtained, entry is permitted. For this reason He said ﴿unless permission is given﴾ without specifying the agent. So if the one giving permission is Allah, or the Prophet, or reason supported by evidence, entry is permitted. The transmitted text indicates this when He, exalted is He, said ﴿or your friends﴾, and the definition of friendship is as we have mentioned. So if Abu Bakr came and knew that there was no impediment in the house of ʿĀʾisha among the houses of the Prophet, peace be upon him, such as exposure or the presence of a non-mahram (a person with whom marriage is forbidden) with her, or if he knew that the house was empty of its household, or if she needed help to extinguish a fire in it or something else, entry would be permitted.

The fourth issue: His saying ﴿and when you have eaten, disperse﴾. Some of the Companions had lingered a long time on the day of the Prophet's banquet at the wedding of Zaynab, peace be upon him, and the Prophet, peace be upon him, said nothing to him. So the verse came comprehensive of etiquettes, among them the prohibition of prolonged stay in people's houses. The meaning of "house" includes any permissible place chosen by a person for his worship or for his occupation, so that someone comes to him and lingers with him. His saying ﴿and do not linger for conversation﴾: al-Zamakhshari said it is a conjunction with ﴿without waiting for its preparation﴾, in the genitive. It may also be in the accusative as a conjunction to the meaning, since the meaning of His saying, exalted is He, ﴿do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless permission is given you﴾ is: do not enter them rushing upon them. So ﴿and do not linger﴾ is conjoined to it. Then Allah, exalted is He, explained that this is an etiquette and that the Prophet is forbearing, by His saying ﴿Indeed, that would cause offense to the Prophet, and he is shy of you, but Allah is not shy of the truth﴾, indicating that this is a right and an etiquette. His saying "kāna" (it would) indicates the Prophet's patience, peace be upon him. Then Allah mentioned another etiquette, which is His saying ﴿And when you ask his wives for something, ask them from behind a screen﴾. When Allah prevented people from entering the houses of the Prophet, peace be upon him, and this made it difficult to reach the ma'un (household necessities), He explained that this is not prohibited, so let one ask and request from behind a screen. His saying ﴿That is purer for your hearts and their hearts﴾ means: the eye is the window of the heart. When the eye does not see, the heart does not desire; but if the eye sees, the heart may or may not desire. So the heart is purer when there is no seeing, and the absence of temptation is then more evident. Then, when Allah, exalted is He, taught the believers the etiquette, He reinforced it with that which moves them to observe it, saying ﴿And it is not for you to offend the Messenger of Allah﴾. Everything you have been forbidden from is an offense, so refrain from it. As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿or to marry his wives after him, ever﴾, it is said that the occasion of its revelation was that a certain man, said to be Talha ibn ʿUbayd Allah, said: "If I live after Muhammad, I will surely marry ʿĀʾisha." We have already mentioned that the occasion of revelation does not restrict the general wording's meaning. The intended meaning is that harming the Messenger is forbidden, and encroaching upon his wives during his lifetime is harm, so it is not permitted. Then He said: No, rather that is impermissible absolutely. He reinforced this with His saying ﴿Indeed, that would be an enormity in the sight of Allah﴾, that is, harming the Messenger.

Then Almighty God said: ﴿If you disclose a thing or conceal it, indeed Allah is ever Knower of all things﴾

Page 195

That is: if you do not harm him (ﷺ) at present, but you resolve to harm him or to marry his wives after him, then Allah is Knowing of what the breasts contain.

ثُمَّ إنَّ اللَّهَ تَعالى لَمّا أنْزَلَ الحِجابَ اسْتَثْنى المَحارِمَ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿لا جُناحَ عَلَيْهِنَّ في آبائِهِنَّ ولا أبْنائِهِنَّ ولا إخْوانِهِنَّ ولا أبْناءِ إخْوانِهِنَّ ولا أبْناءِ أخَواتِهِنَّ ولا نِسائِهِنَّ ولا ما مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُهُنَّ﴾ وفي الآيَةِ مَسائِلُ:

The first issue: In the matter of the veil, Allah made it obligatory upon men to ask [the women] from behind a screen. So why did He not exempt men from the blame, and why did He not say "there is no blame upon them concerning their fathers"? We say: His saying, ﴿فاسْألُوهُنَّ مِن وراءِ حِجابٍ﴾ ("ask them from behind a screen"), is a command to draw the curtain over them, and that cannot happen except when they are concealed and veiled. The veil had already become obligatory upon them, and then He commanded the men to leave them in that state and forbade them from tearing away their coverings. Thus they were exempted in the case of fathers and sons. There is a subtle point here: at the time of the veil, Allah commanded the man to ask from behind a screen, and it is understood from this that the woman is veiled from the man all the more. And at the exemption He said, ﴿لا جُناحَ عَلَيْهِنَّ﴾ ("there is no blame upon them"), when the veil is lifted from them, and men are more entitled to this.

The second issue: He mentioned the fathers first, because their knowledge of their daughters is greater, and how not, when they have seen the whole body of the daughters during their childhood? Then the sons, then the brothers, and this is clear. The discussion concerns the sons of the brothers, since He placed them before the sons of the sisters. This is because the fathers of the sons of the sisters are not mahram (close relatives who are forever unmarriageable, *mahram*) to them; rather they are the husbands of the maternal aunts of those sons. The fathers of the sons of the brothers are also mahram. So there is a certain harm in the sons of the sisters, namely that the son may relate his maternal aunt's affairs to his father, while the father is not a mahram to her, and this is not the case with the sons of the brothers.

The third issue: Allah did not mention the paternal uncles and maternal uncles among the mahram, so He did not say, "nor their paternal uncles or their maternal uncles," for two reasons:

The first: that this is known from the sons of the brothers and the sons of the sisters, because whoever knows that the sons of a brother are mahram to the paternal aunts, knows that the daughters of a brother are mahram to the paternal uncles. The same applies to the maternal uncle.

The second: that paternal uncles may mention the daughters of a brother in front of their sons, while they are not mahram, and the same applies to the son of a maternal uncle.

The fourth issue: ﴿ولا نِسائِهِنَّ﴾ ("nor their women") is attributed to believing women, so that it is not permitted for them to uncover themselves before non-believing women in any respect.

The fifth issue: ﴿ولا ما مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُهُنَّ﴾ ("nor what their right hands possess") comes after all of these, because the harm in uncovering before them is evident. Among the scholars (*a'immah*) there are those who said: what is meant is those who are below the age of puberty.

*

صفحة ١٩٦

Then His saying, ﴿واتَّقِينَ اللَّهَ﴾ ("and fear Allah") in relation to the slaves is evidence that uncovering before them is conditional upon the condition of safety and knowledge that there is no cause for concern. His saying, ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدًا﴾ ("Indeed Allah is ever, over all things, a witness") is most beautiful in this place. This is because what preceded was an indication of the permissibility of seclusion with them and of uncovering before them. So He said: Indeed Allah is a witness when some of you are alone with others. Therefore your privacy is like your gathering, under the witnessing of Allah the Exalted. So fear Him.

* * *

Then He said, ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ ومَلائِكَتَهُ يُصَلُّونَ عَلى النَّبِيِّ﴾ ("Indeed Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet"). When Allah commanded the believers to seek permission and not to gaze at the faces of his wives, out of reverence, He completed the explanation of his sanctity. This is because his state is confined to two situations: the state of his seclusion, and He mentioned what indicates his honour in that state by His saying, ﴿لا تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتَ النَّبِيِّ﴾ ("Do not enter the houses of the Prophet"). And the state in which he is in company, and company is either the exalted assembly (*al-mala' al-a'la*) or the lower assembly (*al-mala' al-adna*). As for the exalted assembly, he is honoured there, for Allah and His angels send blessings upon him. As for the lower assembly, that is a matter of obligatory reverence, by His saying, ﴿ياأيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا صَلُّوا عَلَيْهِ وسَلِّمُوا تَسْلِيمًا﴾ ("O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace"). In this verse there are issues:

The first issue: *al-salah* (prayer) in the language means supplication. It is said: "ṣallā ʿalayhi," meaning he supplicated for him. This meaning is not conceivable with regard to Allah the Exalted, for He does not supplicate for anyone, since supplication for another is a request for his benefit from a third party. Al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, said: the word is used with several meanings, and this has already been discussed in the explanation of His saying, ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي يُصَلِّي عَلَيْكم ومَلائِكَتُهُ﴾ [al-Ahzab: 43] ("It is He who sends blessings upon you, and His angels"). What we add here is that Allah the Exalted said there, ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي يُصَلِّي عَلَيْكم ومَلائِكَتُهُ﴾, making the blessing belong to Allah and joining the angels to Allah. Here He combined Himself and His angels and attributed the blessing to them, saying, ﴿يُصَلُّونَ﴾ ("they send blessings"). In this there is glorification of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. This is because singling out one by mention and joining another to him necessitates preference of the one mentioned over the one joined, just as when a king says, "So-and-so enters, and so-and-so also," there is understood from it a precedence that would not be understood if he said, "So-and-so and so-and-so enter." Knowing this, He said concerning the Prophet, peace be upon him, that they send blessings, as an indication that in blessing the Prophet, peace be upon him, He is like the origin, and in blessing the believers, Allah has mercy on them. Then the angels agree with Him, so they send blessings upon the Prophet, peace be upon him, in addition, as if it were obligatory upon them, or recommended, whether Allah has blessed him or not. In the case of the believers, it is not so.

The second issue: This is evidence for the school of al-Shafi'i, because the command indicates obligation. So the blessing upon the Prophet, peace be upon him, is obligatory, and it is not obligatory outside the tashahhud (the sitting testimony in prayer), so it is obligatory in the tashahhud.

The third issue: The Prophet, peace be upon him, was asked, "How should we send blessings upon you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Say: O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim, and bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed Ibrahim and the family of Ibrahim. We say: the blessing upon him is not because of his need for it, otherwise there would be no need for the angels' blessing alongside Allah's blessing upon him. It is only to show our glorification of Him, out of compassion for us, so that He may reward us for it. صفحة ١٩٧

We say: His saying, ﴿فاسْألُوهُنَّ مِن وراءِ حِجابٍ﴾ ("ask them from behind a screen"), is a command to draw the curtain over them, and that cannot happen except when they are concealed and veiled. Thus they were exempted in the case of fathers and sons. And at the exemption He said, ﴿لا جُناحَ عَلَيْهِنَّ﴾ ("there is no blame upon them"), when the veil is lifted from them, and men are more entitled to this.

The second issue: He mentioned the fathers first, because their knowledge of their daughters is greater, and how not, when they have seen the whole body of the daughters during their childhood? Then the sons, then the brothers, and this is clear. The discussion concerns the sons of the brothers, since He placed them before the sons of the sisters. This is because the fathers of the sons of the sisters are not mahram (close relatives who are forever unmarriageable, *mahram*) to them; rather they are the husbands of the maternal aunts of those sons. The fathers of the sons of the brothers are also mahram. So there is a certain harm in the sons of the sisters, namely that the son may relate his maternal aunt's affairs to his father, while the father is not a mahram to her, and this is not the case with the sons of the brothers.

The third issue: Allah did not mention the paternal uncles and maternal uncles among the mahram, so He did not say, "nor their paternal uncles or their maternal uncles," for two reasons:

The first: that this is known from the sons of the brothers and the sons of the sisters, because whoever knows that the sons of a brother are mahram to the paternal aunts, knows that the daughters of a brother are mahram to the paternal uncles. The same applies to the maternal uncle.

The second: that paternal uncles may mention the daughters of a brother in front of their sons, while they are not mahram, and the same applies to the son of a maternal uncle.

The fourth issue: ﴿ولا نِسائِهِنَّ﴾ ("nor their women") is attributed to believing women, so that it is not permitted for them to uncover themselves before non-believing women in any respect.

The fifth issue: ﴿ولا ما مَلَكَتْ أيْمانُهُنَّ﴾ ("nor what their right hands possess") comes after all of these, because the harm in uncovering before them is evident. Among the scholars (*a'immah*) there are those who said: what is meant is those who are below the age of puberty.

صفحة ١٩٧

Then Almighty God said: ﴿Indeed, those who harm Allah and His Messenger—Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter, and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment.﴾

He distinguished the matters by clarifying some of their opposites. Thus He explained the condition of those who harm the Prophet, so as to show the excellence of the Muslim towards him. Cursing (la'n) is the gravest of the prohibited matters, because distance from God, with which no good is hoped, is different from punishment by the Fire and other things. Do you not see that when a king becomes displeased with a slave, if his being hurt is not severe, he rebukes him and does not expel him? And if the criminal were given the choice between being beaten and being expelled, while the king is at the height of majesty and generosity, he would choose beating over expulsion, especially when there is no king in this world other than his master. His saying ﴿in this world and the Hereafter﴾ indicates a distance with which there is no hope of nearness, because one who is distanced in this world hopes for nearness in the Hereafter; so if he is distanced in the Hereafter, he has failed and lost. For if God distances and expels him, who then brings him near on the Day of Resurrection? Then, He did not confine his recompense to distancing, but threatened him with punishment by His saying: ﴿and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment.﴾ On this there are several issues:

The first issue: He mentioned harming God and harming the Messenger, and after it mentioned two things: cursing and punishment. Cursing is God's recompense, because whoever harms a king distances him from his door, if the king does not command his punishment. Punishment is the recompense for harming the Messenger, because when a king is harmed by one of his great servants, he exacts retribution from him. It may be said: according to this, whoever harms God but does not harm the Messenger is not punished. We say: separating the two in this way is impossible, because whoever harms God has harmed the Messenger. As for the other case, that whoever harms the Prophet ʿalayhi al-salām but does not harm God, like one who disobeys without associating partners, or one who commits sin or immorality without apostasy and disbelief, he has indeed harmed the Prophet ʿalayhi al-salām; yet God is Patient, Forgiving, Merciful, so He recompenses him with punishment and does not curse him by distancing him from the door.

The second issue: He emphasized the punishment by describing it as humiliating, because when a master is hurt by his slave and commands his imprisonment and beating, if he commands his imprisonment in a distinguished place, or commands that he be beaten as a great man, this indicates that the matter is light; but if he commands that he be beaten before a crowd and imprisoned among the corrupt, this indicates the severity of the matter. Whoever among those who harm God and His Messenger is eternal in the Fire will be punished with a humiliating punishment. His saying ﴿He has prepared for them﴾ is for emphasis, because when a master punishes his slave in a state of anger without preparation, it is less than when he prepares for him shackles and chains; for the first, one can say this is the effect of anger, and when anger subsides it passes, but this is not so for the second.

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those who harm the believing men and believing women without their having earned it have certainly borne a slander and a clear sin.﴾

Since God, exalted is He, sends blessings upon His Prophet, the harm done to God is never separate from the harm done to him, for whoever harms God has harmed the Messenger. So God made clear to the believers that if you do what I have commanded you and send blessings upon the Prophet just as I have sent blessings upon him, then your harming (others) will not be separate from harming the Messenger. Thus whoever harms you commits a sin, because your harming is harming the Messenger, just as my harming (someone) is harming him. In sum, since blessings have come from God, the angels, the Messenger and the believers, the harm done by any one of them to another is hardly ever separate from harm to the other, just as is the condition of true friends in friendship.

His saying ﴿without their having earned it﴾ is a safeguard against enjoining good without excessive violence. For whoever is flogged a hundred times for drinking wine, or is subjected to the prescribed punishment of forty for playing backgammon, is harmed without having earned it as well. Whoever is flogged for adultery or for the punishment of drinking is not harmed without having earned it, and it may be said that he is not harmed at all, because that is the correction of the condition of the one who is beaten.

His saying ﴿have certainly borne a slander﴾: buhtan (slander) is falsehood, and it occurs only in speech, whereas harm may occur without speech. So whoever harms a believer by beating him or taking his property has not borne a slander. Therefore we say: the intended meaning is "those who harm the believers by speech." This is because God, exalted is He, wished to show the honour of the believer. So when He mentioned that whoever harms God and His Messenger is cursed, the harm done to God consists in denying God's existence after knowing the proofs of His existence, or associating with Him one who neither sees nor hears, or one who has no power and no knowledge, or one who in his existence needs a originator. This is a statement which mentions the harming of the believer by speech. On this basis, the Prophets were singled out for mention with speech, because it is more general and more complete. This is because a human being cannot harm God by that which pains Him, such as beating or taking what He needs; so he harms Him by speech. Also, a poor absent person cannot be harmed by action, but he can be harmed by speech, by saying about him what reaches him so that he is hurt.

The second answer to the question is that we say: His saying afterwards ﴿and a clear sin﴾ is an addition, as if He had said: "They have borne a slander if it is by speech, and a clear sin however the harm is done." And however it is done, God singled out verbal harm for mention, since we have shown that it is more general and because it is more complete, for it reaches the heart. Speech comes out from the heart, and the tongue is its indicator, and it enters the heart, and the ears are its pathway.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 33, verses 59–60:

Then the Exalted said: ﴿O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to draw their outer garments over themselves. That is more suitable that they will be known and not be abused.﴾

When He mentioned that whoever harms the believers bears a calumny, and this entails prohibiting the accountable person from harming the believer, He commanded the believers to avoid the places in which there are accusations that cause harm, so that the prohibited harm does not occur. Since verbal harm is specifically mentioned, He singled out the thing that is the cause of verbal harm, which is women, for their mention in an evil manner harms men and women alike. This is unlike the mention of men, for whoever mentions a woman in an evil manner, she is harmed and her relatives are harmed even more than she is; and whoever mentions a man in an evil manner, he is harmed, but his women are not harmed. In the Jahiliyyah, free women and slave women would go out uncovered, followed by fornicators, and accusations would arise. So God commanded free women to draw their outer garments over themselves (tajalbub).

As for His words: ﴿That is more suitable that they will be known and not be abused﴾, it has been said: they will be known as free women, so they will not be followed. It is also possible to say: the meaning is that they will be known as not being fornicators, because one who covers her face, although the face is not an 'awrah, is not hoped to be one who uncovers her 'awrah, so they are known as being chaste, and it is not possible to seek fornication from them.

His words: ﴿And God is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ means He forgives you what has passed by His mercy and rewards you for what you do, being merciful to you.

﴿If the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is a disease and those who spread rumors in the city do not cease, We will surely incite you against them; then they will not remain your neighbors therein except for a little.﴾

When He mentioned the state of the polytheist who harms God and His Messenger, and the open offender who harms the believers, He mentioned the state of the secret one who shows the truth and conceals falsehood, namely the hypocrite. Since what was mentioned earlier were three groups, in view of three considerations—namely those who harm God, those who harm the Messenger, and those who harm the believers—He mentioned three of the secret ones, in view of three considerations:

The first: the hypocrite who harms God secretly.

The second: the one in whose heart is a disease, who harms the believer by pursuing his women.

The third: the rumor-spreader who harms the Prophet, peace be upon him, by spreading rumors saying: Muhammad has been defeated, and he will leave Medina, and he will be captured. Although these are one group, they have three considerations. This is in contrast to His words: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women…﴾ [al-Ahzab: 35], where He mentioned ten categories, all of which exist in one person; so they are one in person and many in consideration.

His words: ﴿We will surely incite you against them﴾ mean: We will surely give you power over them and We will surely expel them from Medina. Then they will not remain your neighbors, and Medina will be emptied of them by death or expulsion. It is also possible that the meaning is: We will surely incite you against them, so when We incite you, they will not remain your neighbors. The first is like the saying of one who says: "So-and-so goes out and recites," indicating two matters; and the second is like His saying: "So-and-so goes out and enters the market," where in the first he recites even if he does not go out, and in the second he does not enter except if he goes out.

The exception here contains a subtle point, namely that God the Exalted promised the Prophet, peace be upon him, that He would expel his enemies from Medina and remove them at his hand, to manifest his might. Had the expulsion been by the will of God without the intermediary of the Prophet, He would have emptied Medina of them in the most subtle moment, by His saying "Be," and it would be. But since God willed that it be at the hand of the Prophet, it would not occur except after a time, however brief. So He said: ﴿Then they will not remain your neighbors therein except for a little﴾, which is the time in which they prepare and make ready for departure.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 33, verses 64–68:

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, God has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a blazing Fire﴾ ﴿abiding therein forever﴾. He means: just as they are cursed among you in this world, so they are cursed before God. ﴿And He has prepared for them a blazing Fire﴾, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿God has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter, and has prepared for them a humiliating punishment﴾ [al-Ahzab: 57]. ﴿Abiding therein forever﴾: remaining there for a long time, continuing, with no end to their departure.

His saying: ﴿They will find no protector or helper﴾. When He mentioned their eternal abiding, He clarified its reality. This is because the one being punished is not freed from the punishment except by a friend who intercedes for him or a helper who repels it from him, and there is no protector for them to intercede, nor a helper to repel.

﴿On the Day their faces are turned over in the Fire, they will say: "Oh, would that we had obeyed God and obeyed the Messenger!"﴾ ﴿And they will say: "Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our leaders and our elders, and they misled us from the way."﴾ ﴿Our Lord, give them double the punishment and curse them with a great curse.﴾

Having explained that they have no intercessor who will repel the punishment from them, He explained that some of their limbs also cannot repel the punishment from others. This is unlike the punishment of this world, for a person protects his face from a blow by his hand, since whoever aims at a man's head and face finds him placing his hand as a shield (junnah) or lowering his head so that the blow does not strike his face. In the Hereafter, ﴿their faces are turned over in the Fire﴾. So what do you think of the rest of their limbs, which in this world serve as a shield and protection for the face? ﴿They say: "Oh, would that we had obeyed God and obeyed the Messenger!"﴾ They lament and regret, but regret and lamentation will not benefit them, since they have come to know that salvation is only for the obedient.

Then they say: ﴿Indeed, we obeyed our leaders and our elders﴾, meaning: instead of obeying God, the Exalted, we obeyed the leaders, and instead of obeying the Messenger, we obeyed the elders, and we abandoned obedience to the Master of masters and the Greatest of the great. Thus we exchanged good for evil, so surely the good of the Gardens escaped us, and we were given the evil of the Fires.

Then they seek some satisfaction by punishing the misleaders, and they say: ﴿Our Lord, give them double the punishment and curse them with a great curse﴾, that is, because of their misguidance and their misleading of others.

In His saying, exalted is He: ﴿double﴾ and ﴿curse them with a great curse﴾ there is a subtle meaning, which is that supplication occurs only when the thing requested has not yet been obtained. The punishment was already present for them, and so was the curse. Yet they asked for what was not yet present: an increase in punishment, by their saying ﴿double﴾, and an increase in the curse, by their saying ﴿a great curse﴾.
