Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿O you who believe, do not be like those who abused Moses, but Allah cleared him of what they said.﴾

When Allah, exalted is He, made clear that whoever harms Allah and His Messenger will be cursed and punished, and that this was an allusion to harm that amounts to disbelief, He guided the believers to refrain from harm that is less than that and does not result in disbelief. This is like one who is not content with the Prophet's distribution (qasm) and his judgment regarding the fay' (spoils that came without fighting) for some people, and other such things. So He said: ﴿O you who believe, do not be like those who abused Moses﴾. The account of the abuse of Moses is subject to difference of opinion. Some said it was their harming him by attributing to him a defect in his body. Others said: Qarun arranged with a wicked woman that she would say in front of the Children of Israel, "Moses committed adultery with me." When Qarun gathered the people, with the woman present, Allah cast into her heart that she should tell the truth, and she did not say what she had been coached to say. In general, the abuse mentioned in the Qur'an is sufficient, namely that they said to him: ﴿So go, you and your Lord, and fight [both of you]﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 24], and their saying: ﴿We will never believe you until we see Allah openly﴾ [al-Baqarah: 55], and their saying: ﴿We will never endure one kind of food﴾ [al-Baqarah: 61], and so on. So He said to the believers: Do not be like them when the Messenger calls you to fighting; that is, do not say, "So go, you and your Lord, and fight," and do not ask for what has not been permitted to you. [The Prophet said]: "When I command you to do something, do of it what you are able."

As for His saying: ﴿but Allah cleared him of what they said﴾, according to the first view it is clear, since He made his body appear to his people, so they saw him and knew the corruption of their belief, and the woman spoke the truth; and He commanded the angels, so they passed by him with Aaron, and they saw him undamaged, so they knew the innocence of Moses, peace be upon him, from the killing with which they had accused him. According to what we have mentioned, ﴿Allah cleared him of what they said﴾ means He freed him from the obligation of what they demanded by giving them part of it and showing that it was not permissible to give part of it. In sum, Allah cut off their argument, then imposed upon them humiliation and wretchedness and was angry with them.

His saying: ﴿and he was honourable in the sight of Allah﴾ means he was of high standing (wajahah) and recognition. The wajih is the man who has a face, that is, who is known for good. Although everyone is known to Allah, mere recognition is not sufficient for standing (wajahah), for one who is known to others merely because he serves someone or is employed by him is not called "of standing with so-and-so." Rather, the one of standing is one who has praiseworthy qualities that make his status such that he is recognised and not denied. And he was like that.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 33, verse 72:

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice﴾ ﴿He will amend for you your deeds and forgive you your sins﴾. He guided them to what should proceed from them of actions and statements. As for actions, it is goodness; as for statements, it is truth, because whoever brings goodness and abandons evil has feared Allah, and whoever speaks the truth has spoken words of appropriate justice. Then He promised them for both matters with two things: for the goodnesses, the amendment of their deeds, for by the fear of Allah deeds are made sound, and sound deeds are raised up and endure, so their doer remains eternal in Paradise; and for the appropriate speech, the forgiveness of sins.
* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly achieved a great attainment﴾. The obedience to Allah is the obedience to the Messenger, but He combined them to show the nobility of the act of the one who obeys; for if one person does it, he has taken a covenant with Allah and a favour with the Messenger. His saying ﴿has certainly achieved a great attainment﴾ made it great in two respects:

The first: that it is from a great punishment, and salvation from punishment grows in greatness with the greatness of the punishment, to the extent that if someone wished to strike another with a whip and then was saved from it, it would not be said he achieved a great attainment; because the punishment from which he was saved, had it occurred, the matter would not have differed greatly.

The second: that he has reached great reward, which is the eternal, everlasting reward.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it; and man bore it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant﴾.

When Allah guided the believers to noble characteristics and disciplined the Prophet, peace be upon him, with the best of manners, He made clear that the obligation which Allah directed to man is a great matter. So He said: ﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust﴾, that is, the obligation, which is the command contrary to what is in nature. Know that this kind of obligation is not in the heavens nor in the earth, because the earth, the mountain and the heaven are all as they were created: the mountain is not asked to walk, the earth is not asked to ascend, nor the heaven to descend; and not among the angels, because although the angels are commanded and forbidden in things, these are for them as eating and drinking are for us, so they glorify night and day without slackening, just as a person occupies himself with a matter that suits his nature. In the verse there are issues:

The first issue: concerning the Trust there are many aspects. Among them, one who said: it is the obligation, and it was called a trust because whoever falls short in it bears a penalty, and whoever fulfils it has honour. Among them, one who said it is the statement "there is no god but Allah", and this is far-fetched, for the heavens, the earth and the mountains with their tongues testify that Allah is One, there is no god but Him. Among them, one who said: the members; the eye is a trust which one should guard, and the ear likewise, and the hand likewise, and the foot and the private parts and the tongue. Among them, one who said: the knowledge of Allah with what is in it. And Allah knows best.

The second issue: concerning the offering there are aspects. Among them, one who said: what is meant is the offering; among them, one who said: the gathering; among them, one who said: the presentation, i.e., We presented the Trust to the heavens, and the Trust outweighed the people of the heavens and the earth.

The third issue: ﴿to the heavens and the earth﴾ has two aspects:

One: that what is meant is they themselves in their very substance.

The second: what is meant is their inhabitants, so there is an implied element, its estimate being: Indeed, We offered the Trust to the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth.

The fourth issue: His saying ﴿but they declined to bear it﴾ — their refusal was not like the refusal of Iblis in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He refused to be among those who prostrate﴾ [al-Hijr: 31], in two respects:

One: that there, prostration was an obligation, whereas here the Trust was an offering.

The second: that the refusal there was out of arrogance, whereas here it was out of humility; they regarded themselves as small, as shown by His saying: ﴿and feared it﴾.

The fifth issue: What is the cause of the fear? We say: the Trust is not accepted for several reasons:

The first: that it is precious and hard to keep, like vessels made of jewels, which are precious and quick to break; a sensible person refrains from accepting them. If they were of gold or silver he would accept them, and if they were of glass he would accept them: in the first case because of his safety from their destruction, and in the second because they are not rare in existence. The obligation is likewise.

The second: that the time is a time of meteors and raids, so a sensible person does not accept deposits at such a time, and the matter was thus, because Satan and his hosts were targeting the accountable, since the purpose was after Adam's departure from Paradise.

The third: the observance of the trust and the performance of what is required, such as the deposit of animals which need fodder and water and a specific place suited to them; a sensible person refrains from accepting them, unlike goods placed in a chest or in a corner of a house. The obligation is likewise, for it requires nurture and development.

The sixth issue: How did man bear it when these things did not bear it? There are two answers:

One: because of his ignorance of what it contains and their knowledge, which is why He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant﴾.

The second: that the things looked at themselves, saw their weakness and refrained, whereas man looked at the side of the one imposing the obligation and said: the Depositor is knowing and capable, He offers the trust only to its people, and when He deposits, He does not abandon it, but preserves it by His sight and His help; so he accepted it, and said: ﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾ [al-Fatihah: 5].

The seventh issue: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant﴾ has aspects:

One: that what is meant by it is Adam, who wronged himself by disobedience and did not know the punishment for it, namely the expulsion from Paradise.

Second: what is meant is man, who wrongs by disobedience and is ignorant of the punishment upon him.

Third: "Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant" means that it was in his nature to be unjust and ignorant. It is said: a horse that bucks (shamus), a beast that runs wild (jamuh), water that purifies (tahur), meaning that it is its nature to be so. Likewise man's nature is injustice and ignorance; when the Trust was deposited with him, some remained as they were, and some left injustice as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Those who have believed and have not mixed their belief with injustice﴾ [al-An'am: 82], and left ignorance as He, exalted is He, said concerning Adam, peace be upon him: ﴿And He taught Adam the names, all of them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 31], and said concerning the believers in general: ﴿And those firm in knowledge say: We believe in it﴾ [Al 'Imran: 7], and He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Only those of His servants who have knowledge fear Allah﴾ [Fatir: 28].

Fourth: ﴿Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant﴾ in the view of the angels, when they said: ﴿Will You place therein one who causes corruption therein?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 30], and He showed His knowledge among them when He said, exalted is He: ﴿Inform Me of the names of these﴾ [al-Baqarah: 31]. Some of them said in interpreting the verse: created beings are of two kinds: perceiving and non-perceiving. Among the perceiving are those who perceive both universals and particulars, like the human being; and among them are those who perceive particulars only, like cattle, which perceive the barley they eat but do not reflect on the consequences of matters nor consider proofs and evidences; and among them are those who perceive universals but do not perceive particulars, like the angel, which perceives universals but does not perceive the pleasure of intercourse and eating. They said: Allah, exalted is He, indicated this by His saying: ﴿Then He presented them to the angels and said, "Inform Me of the names of these"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 31], so they acknowledged their lack of knowledge of those particulars. The obligation applies only to one who perceives both matters, since he has pleasures in particular things, so he is restrained from them in order to attain true pleasures, like the pleasure of the angels in worshipping Allah and knowing Him. As for others, if they are accountable, they are accountable not in the sense of a command containing hardship and difficulty for them, but in the sense of address, for the one addressed is called accountable, since the accountable is one addressed; thus the one addressed is called accountable.

In the verse there are subtleties:

The first: the Trust was offered to Adam, and he accepted it, and so he was trustworthy regarding it, and the word of the trustworthy is accepted, so he was successful. His descendants then took the trust from him, and the one who takes from the trustworthy is not himself trusted; for this reason, the heir of the depositor does not have his word accepted, and he had no choice but to renew a covenant and trust. The believer has taken a covenant with Allah, so he became trustworthy from Allah, and his word became accepted, so he had what Adam had of success. For this reason He, exalted is He, said: ﴿and Allah will turn in forgiveness to the believing men and believing women﴾ [al-Ahzab: 73], that is, as He turned in forgiveness to Adam in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then his Lord accepted his repentance﴾ [al-Baqarah: 37]. The disbeliever has become one who takes the trust from the trusted, so it remains under his responsibility. Then if something of the trust in the believer's hand is lost by the decree and destiny of Allah, it is without fault on his part, and the trustworthy does not bear liability for what is lost without fault; but if something of the trust in the disbeliever's hand is lost, he is liable even if it was by the decree and destiny of Allah, because he is liable for what is lost even if it was not through negligence.

The second subtlety: He singled out the three things for mention because they are the greatest of things and the most able to bear weights. As for the heavens, that is due to His saying: ﴿And We built above you seven strong heavens﴾ [al-Naba': 12]; and the earth and the mountains, their strength and hardness are not hidden. Further, since these things had strength and hardness, Allah offered the Trust to them and was satisfied with their strength and power, but they refrained, because although they were strong, the trust of Allah, exalted is He, is above their strength. Man bore it despite his weakness, of which Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And man was created weak﴾ [al-Nisa': 28]; yet He promised him help in preserving the trust by His saying: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, He is sufficient for him﴾ [al-Talaq: 3]. If it is said: how is the one whom Allah helps punished, and why does He punish the disbeliever? We say: Allah, exalted is He, said: "I help the one who seeks My help and relies upon Me." The disbeliever did not turn to Allah, exalted is He, so He left him to himself, and he remains under the obligation of the trust.

The third subtlety: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿but they declined to bear it﴾ and His saying: ﴿and man bore it﴾ indicates that there is hardship in it, unlike if He had said: "they declined to accept it and man accepted it." Whoever says to another: do this act, and if the act involves no toil that is matched by a wage, then when he does it he does not deserve a wage. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿and bore it﴾, indicating that it is something for which one deserves a reward, that is, for the mere bearing of the trust; and as for preserving it in the fullest sense of preservation, one deserves additional reward. If it is said: all of them bore it; the most that can be said is that the disbeliever did not add anything beyond the bearing, so he should deserve a reward for the bearing. We say: when an act is done in accordance with the permission of the owner who commanded it, the doer deserves a wage. Do you not see that if he said: "Carry this to the estate that is to the north," and he carried it and transported it to the estate that is to the south, he does not deserve a wage, and he is obliged to return it to the place where it was? Likewise the disbeliever bore it not in accordance with the permission, so he is liable, and his good deeds which he performed because of it are lost.

Then He said, exalted is He: ﴿That Allah may punish the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women, and the polytheist men and the polytheist women, and that Allah may turn in forgiveness to the believing men and the believing women. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

That is, man bore it so that the punishment of the hypocrite and the polytheist would come to pass. If someone asks: why did He mention the punishment before the repentance? We say: since He named the moral obligation (taklif) a trust (amanah), and among the necessary rulings of a trust is that the one who betrays it is liable, while it is not a necessary ruling of a trust that the faithful person who exerts his utmost effort receives a wage, then punishment for betrayal was like a necessary consequence, whereas the reward for preserving the trust is a kindness (ihsan), and justice comes before kindness. There are two issues (masa'il) in this:

The First Issue: Why did He join the polytheist to the hypocrite without repeating His name, so that He did not say, "and Allah punishes the polytheists," whereas at the repentance He repeated His name and said, "and Allah turns in forgiveness"? If He had said, "and turns in forgiveness to the believers," the meaning would have been achieved. We say: He intended to give precedence to the believer over the hypocrite, so He made it like a new independent sentence (kalam mustaʾnaf), and there the agent had to be mentioned, so He said, ﴿and Allah turns﴾. This is confirmed by the reading of the one who read (wa-yatubu Allahu) with a nominative ending (raf').

[Page 205]

The Second Issue: Allah mentioned two attributes of man: "zalum" (wrongdoing, a great wrongdoer) and "jahul" (ignorant), and He mentioned two of His own attributes, saying: ﴿And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾. That is, He is forgiving toward the wrongdoer and merciful toward the ignorant. This is because Allah, exalted is He, promised His servants that He forgives all wrongdoing except the great wrongdoing, which is polytheism, as He said: ﴿Indeed, polytheism is a great wrong﴾ [Luqman: 13]. As for the promise, it is His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with; but He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills﴾ [al-Nisa': 48]. As for mercy toward ignorance, it is because ignorance is the locus of mercy, and for this reason the wrongdoer excuses himself by saying: "I did not know."

Here is a subtle point: Allah, exalted is He, informed His servant that He is Forgiving and Merciful, and showed him his own self, so he saw himself as a wrongdoer and ignorant. Then He offered him the trust, and he accepted it despite his wrongdoing and ignorance, because of His knowledge that He would compensate for it with forgiveness and mercy. And Allah knows best.

All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah send blessings upon Muhammad, the unlettered Prophet, and upon his family.
